bugs.creator: kevinushey
bugs.summary: chartr() and case conversion read past utf8_table2 on UTF-8-marked strings with 0xFF runs (utf8toucs decodes 5/6-byte forms unchecked)

comments.text:
utf8toucs() in src/main/util.c decodes the withdrawn 5- and 6-byte UTF-8 forms "with no testing": it neither checks the continuation bytes nor masks the lead byte to the bits those forms carry. A run of 0xFF bytes is therefore accepted as a 6-byte sequence whose value overflows 31 bits, and Rwcrtomb32() then reads one element past utf8_table2 when encoding it back. Any UTF-8-marked string can hold such bytes (the mark is not validated), and chartr(), toupper(), tolower() and casefold() all go through this code.

Reproducible example:

x <- "J\xff\xff\xff\xff z"
Encoding(x) <- "UTF-8"
chartr("a", "b", x)

Observed (R 4.6.1 and R-devel r90646): [1] "J\xff\xbf\xbf\xbf\xbf\xa0\xba" -- garbage, with the trailing " z" lost. Under AddressSanitizer:

==1==ERROR: AddressSanitizer: global-buffer-overflow
READ of size 4
    #0 Rwcrtomb32      src/main/util.c:1551
    #1 Rf_wcstoutf8    src/main/util.c:1580
    #2 do_chartr       src/main/character.c:1630

Expected: the "invalid input in 'utf8towcs'" error that runs of 1-3 or 7+ such bytes already produce.

Analysis:

utf8toucs() validates 2- to 4-byte sequences but masks a 5- or 6-byte lead with 0x0F and never checks what follows, so an 0xFF lead contributes 0xF << 30. Rwcrtomb32() searches utf8_table1 (largest entry 0x7FFFFFFF), runs off the end with i == 6, and reads utf8_table2[6]. The 5-byte branch also shifts its first two continuation bytes by the same amount (12 and 12 rather than 18 and 12), so it has never decoded those sequences correctly.

Proposed patch: attached as utf8toucs-long-sequences.diff. It checks the 5- and 6-byte forms like the shorter ones (continuation bytes must be 10xxxxxx, the lead byte contributes only its low 2 or 1 bits, 0xFE and 0xFF are rejected), fixes the 5-byte shift, and makes Rwcrtomb32() refuse values above 0x7FFFFFFF as a backstop. With it, an ASAN build raises the utf8towcs error for every 0xFF run length, and valid 5/6-byte forms and ordinary UTF-8 are unchanged.

Found by fuzzing R with libFuzzer + AddressSanitizer (r-devel/r-oss-fuzz).

The patch is also submitted as https://github.com/r-devel/r-svn/pull/360, where CI results can be seen.
